lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt:
For a real square matrix $A$, a non-zero vector $v$ is an eigenvector when

$$Av=\lambda v.$$

The scalar $\lambda$ is its associated eigenvalue. The non-zero requirement matters: the zero vector satisfies the equation for every scalar and therefore carries no information about a special direction.

$$A=Q\Lambda Q^T,\qquad \Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n).$$
